Key_Symptoms: Dry eyes, foamy white patches on conjunctiva, mild photophobia
Visible_Ocular_Signs: Foamy/triangular white-gray patches on bulbar conjunctiva (Bitot spots), conjunctival dryness
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Night blindness, dry skin, frequent infections, poor wound healing
Risk_Factors: Malnutrition, low dietary intake of leafy greens/dairy/liver, chronic diarrhea, malabsorption disorders

Key_Symptoms: Dryness and grittiness in eyes, redness, irritation
Visible_Ocular_Signs: Dull, dry, non-wettable conjunctiva, loss of normal luster, wrinkled appearance
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Night blindness, dry/rough skin (phrynoderma), reduced immunity
Risk_Factors: Vitamin A deficient diet, fat malabsorption, alcoholism, liver disease

Key_Symptoms: Severe dryness, eye pain, blurred vision, light sensitivity
Visible_Ocular_Signs: Dry, hazy, lusterless cornea; loss of corneal transparency
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Night blindness progressing to daytime vision issues, growth retardation in children
Risk_Factors: Prolonged untreated Vit A deficiency, malnutrition in children, measles infection

Key_Symptoms: Severe eye pain, excessive tearing, vision loss, sensitivity to light
Visible_Ocular_Signs: Open sore/ulcer on cornea, corneal clouding, possible discharge
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Fever (if infected), severe malnutrition signs, weight loss
Risk_Factors: Untreated xerophthalmia, secondary bacterial infection, severe pediatric malnutrition

Key_Symptoms: Rapid vision loss, eye pain, corneal softening sensation
Visible_Ocular_Signs: Softening and necrosis of cornea, corneal perforation risk, cloudy/melting appearance
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Severe malnutrition, stunted growth, high infection susceptibility, immune suppression
Risk_Factors: Advanced untreated Vit A deficiency, severe pediatric malnutrition, measles co-infection

Key_Symptoms: Blurred/reduced vision, visible white mark on eye, light sensitivity
Visible_Ocular_Signs: Permanent white/grayish scarring on cornea, irregular corneal surface
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: History of prior corneal ulceration, residual vision impairment
Risk_Factors: Sequela of untreated corneal xerosis/ulceration, chronic Vit A deficiency

Key_Symptoms: Gradual painless vision loss, blurred central vision, difficulty distinguishing colors
Visible_Ocular_Signs: Optic disc pallor, swelling of optic nerve head, reduced visual acuity, central/cecocentral scotoma
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Fatigue, numbness/tingling in hands and feet, memory issues, glossitis, pale skin, anemia
Risk_Factors: Vegan/vegetarian diet, pernicious anemia, gastric bypass surgery, elderly age, metformin use, alcoholism

Vitamin_Deficiency: Multiple (B1, B2, B6, B9, Folate) Deficiency
Key_Symptoms: Progressive blurred vision, dimming of vision, color vision changes
Visible_Ocular_Signs: Optic disc pallor or edema, bilateral symmetric vision loss, visual field defects
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Peripheral neuropathy, fatigue, poor appetite, irritability, glossitis, weakness
Risk_Factors: Chronic alcoholism, poor diet, malabsorption syndromes, bariatric surgery, smoking combined with poor nutrition

Visible_Ocular_Signs: Clear cornea, healthy moist conjunctiva, normal optic disc, no abnormal pigmentation or lesions

Key_Symptoms: Blurred vision, floaters, fluctuating vision, dark spots in vision
Visible_Ocular_Signs: Microaneurysms, retinal hemorrhages, cotton wool spots, neovascularization
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: History of diabetes mellitus, poor glycemic control, fatigue, frequent urination
Risk_Factors: Long-standing diabetes, poor blood sugar control, hypertension, high cholesterol

Key_Symptoms: Gradual peripheral vision loss, eye pain (acute type), halos around lights
Visible_Ocular_Signs: Elevated intraocular pressure, optic disc cupping, visual field loss
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Headache (acute angle-closure type), nausea in acute cases
Risk_Factors: Age over 60, family history, high eye pressure, certain ethnic backgrounds

Key_Symptoms: Blurred or distorted central vision, difficulty reading/recognizing faces
Visible_Ocular_Signs: Drusen deposits, retinal pigment changes, geographic atrophy or neovascularization
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Age over 50, difficulty with central vision tasks
Risk_Factors: Advanced age, smoking, family history, cardiovascular disease

Key_Symptoms: Cloudy/blurry vision, glare sensitivity, faded color perception
Visible_Ocular_Signs: Lens opacity/cloudiness visible on examination, reduced red reflex
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Difficulty with night driving, frequent prescription changes
Risk_Factors: Aging, prolonged UV exposure, diabetes, smoking, steroid use

Key_Symptoms: Often asymptomatic early, blurred vision in advanced stages, headache
Visible_Ocular_Signs: Arteriolar narrowing, AV nicking, retinal hemorrhages, papilledema in severe cases
Risk_Factors: Chronic uncontrolled high blood pressure, atherosclerosis
